Its thermodynamic projection is $\Pi(\mathcal F):=\{\mathbf x\in\mathcal D:\exists\mathbf y\text{ with }(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\in\mathcal F\}$; that projection alone does not record variable auxiliary states, energy or entropy. When $k=0$ the original convention $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal D$ applies. Totals use all supplied endpoint maps and the dimensioned coordinate maps $U_c,V_c,n_{c,j}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], rather than treating numerical coordinates as quantities with units. For two constituents without auxiliaries, thermal contact through [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]] at fixed volumes and mole amounts gives the model-declared allowed energy partitions with prescribed total energy and any further retained constraints. Volume or species exchange changes $\mathcal F$ only when explicitly permitted; retained walls fix the corresponding coordinates.

downstream_reviews.exact_snippet:
For complete contact data, set $E:=(0,3/10]\cup[3/5,9/10]$ and take $Z_{A\sqcup B}=Z_{A\sqcup B}^{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal F$, with constituent maps $\xi_A,\xi_B$ the two coordinate projections and contact family $\mathcal T:=\{(c_A,x_A):x_A\in D_A\}\cup\{(c_B,x_B):x_B\in D_B\}$. The two constitutions share one species label. Give the aggregate constitution the domain $D_{A\sqcup B}=(0,\infty)^3$, and set $\xi_{A\sqcup B}(\phi(x))=(1,\hat V_A+\hat V_B,\hat n_A+\hat n_B)$. This is a supplied aggregate coordinate map for process records, not an assertion of an aggregate entropy identity. For each $x,y\in E$ with $y\ge x$, admit the record $P_{x,y}$ of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]] on $I=[0,1]$ seconds: its aggregate endpoints are both this constant coordinate tuple, $z_{x,y}(t)=\phi(x)$ for $0\le t<1$ and $z_{x,y}(1)=\phi(y)$, its control record is $(x,y)$, and its signed transfer record is the real number $x-y$. Declare the control-record set to be $\{(x,y)\in E^2:y\ge x\}$ and the transfer-record set to be $\mathbb R$. No path regularity is required by the supplier. The outer boundary admits no matter or energy transfer; fixed constituent volumes and amounts and zero contact work are retained constraints. Supply fixed positive constituent and compound masses and zero endpoint center-of-mass velocities in one Galilean chart, and no separately tracked external-field energy. Thus these are core closed records, with $Q[P_{x,y}]=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P_{x,y}]=0$. For the contact-record set $\mathcal P_T=\{P_{x,y}:x,y\in E,\ y\ge x\}$ supply $q_{A\to B}[P_{x,y}]=x-y$ in joule magnitudes as in [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]]. The constituent energy changes are $(y-x)\,\mathrm J$ and $(x-y)\,\mathrm J$. Each feasible endpoint has its self-record; nonzero transfers occur when $y>x$. No contact-equilibrium designation or relaxation law is assumed.

To check consistency with the separately scoped aggregate postulates, take $\mathcal C_{AB}:=\{(x_A,x_B)\in D_A\times D_B:\hat U_A=\hat U_B\}$ and let $\kappa_{AB}$ sum their three coordinates. Adopt $S_{A\sqcup B}(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=\tfrac32s_*\hat U$. On this nonempty admission set, $S_A+S_B=3s_*\hat U_A=S_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))$, and all dimensioned coordinates add. Use the same aggregate formula on its scaled tags and all positive-coordinate scaling domains. The retained partitions in $\mathcal F$ have $x\ne1/2$ and are outside this aggregate admission set, so their separately adopted product entropy does not contradict the aggregate identity. Totals and entropy on these complete partitioned endpoints are additional declared maps allowed by [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The maximum criterion of [[post-td-entropy-maximum]] is used on their stated entropy sum; no aggregate-composition or accessibility theorem is claimed.

**Given:** The equilibrium-coordinate convention of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], the contact restrictions of [[def-td-thermal-contact-constraints]], the feasible-set definition [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]], and the entropy and equilibrium-maximum postulates.

[F7] An equilibrium feasible set is a model-declared subset satisfying the stated totals and retained constraints; the definition imposes no convexity on it ([[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]).

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Assume that, for every phase pair and each of energy, volume, and every named species, the feasible set contains the pairwise transfer curve for all sufficiently small transfers of either sign, varying only the selected coordinate in those two phases with opposite increments and holding every other state coordinate of both phases, all other phases, and all auxiliaries fixed, and every listed reaction direction is feasible in both extent directions in every phase while that phase's energy, volume, other reaction extents, and all other phase coordinates are held fixed at the coexistence point. Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.
